source_reference: Foret, Kleiner, Mobahi, Neyshabur, Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Efficiently Improving Generalization (ICLR 2021), Appendix Theorem 2

problem.description: Given a training dataset S := union_{i=1}^n {(x_i,y_i)} drawn i.i.d. from distribution D, the paper considers a family of models parameterized by w in W subseteq R^d and a per-data-point loss l : W x X x Y -> R_+, then defines the training set loss L_{\mathcal S}(w) := (1/n) sum_i l(w,x_i,y_i) and population loss L_D(w) := E_(x,y)~D[l(w,x,y)].

assumptions.name: IID_Training_Set
assumptions.math: \text{Given a training dataset }\mathcal S \triangleq \bigcup_{i=1}^{n} \{(x_i,y_i)\}\text{ drawn i.i.d. from distribution }\mathcal{D},\text{ we seek to learn a model that generalizes well.}
assumptions.description: This is the paper's complete opening dataset statement; the subsequent setup specifies the model family, loss function, and empirical/population losses.

assumptions.name: Finite_Sample_And_Parameter_Count
assumptions.math: n=|\mathcal S|,\quad k\text{ is the number of parameters}

steps.name: batch_gradient
steps.math: \text{Compute gradient }\nabla_wL_B(w)\text{ of the batch's training loss}

main_theorem.statement_math: \text{Theorem 2. For any }\rho>0\text{ and any distribution }\mathcal D,\text{ with probability }1-\delta\text{ over the choice of the training set }\mathcal S\sim\mathcal D,\quad L_{\mathcal D}(w)\leq\max_{\|\epsilon\|_2\leq\rho}L_{\mathcal S}(w+\epsilon)+\sqrt{\frac{k\log\left(1+\frac{\|w\|_2^2}{\rho^2}\left(1+\sqrt{\frac{\log(n)}{k}}\right)^2\right)+4\log\frac{n}{\delta}+\widetilde O(1)}{n-1}},\quad\text{where }n=|\mathcal S|,\ k\text{ is the number of parameters and we assumed }L_{\mathcal D}(w)\leq\mathbb E_{\epsilon_i\sim\mathcal N(0,\rho)}[L_{\mathcal D}(w+\epsilon)].
main_theorem.statement_ref: Theorem 2, equation (4), Appendix A.1, PDF pp. 14-15 (lines 831-841)
main_theorem.rate: sharpness-neighborhood empirical loss plus O(sqrt((k log(1+(||w||_2^2/rho^2)(1+sqrt(log n/k))^2)+log(n/delta))/n))
main_theorem.measure: population loss L_D(w) with probability 1-delta over S

proof.description: The theorem's right-hand side is lower bounded by the displayed square-root term.
proof.produces: Reduction to the case ||w||_2^2 <= rho^2(exp(4n/k)-1).

proof.description: When ||w||_2^2 exceeds rho^2(exp(4n/k)-1), the lower bound is greater than one and the claim is trivial.
proof.produces: Trivial case discharged.

proof.description: Restrict the remainder of the proof to the complementary norm case.
proof.produces: Reduced case for the PAC-Bayes construction.

proof.description: Invoke McAllester's PAC-Bayesian bound for any prior P and posterior Q.
proof.math: \mathbb E_{w\sim\mathcal Q}[L_{\mathcal D}(w)]\leq\mathbb E_{w\sim\mathcal Q}[L_{\mathcal S}(w)]+\sqrt{\frac{\operatorname{KL}(\mathcal Q\|\mathcal P)+\log\frac n\delta}{2(n-1)}}
proof.produces: PAC-Bayes expectation bound parameterized by P,Q.

proof.description: For isotropic Gaussian P and Q, substitute the closed form KL divergence.
proof.produces: Explicit KL objective in sigma_P, sigma_Q, mu_P, mu_Q.

proof.description: Differentiating the Gaussian KL with respect to sigma_P and setting the derivative to zero gives the unique stationary-point minimizer printed in the paper.
proof.produces: Unconstrained optimal prior variance.

proof.description: The prior must be chosen before observing S, while mu_Q and sigma_Q may depend on S, so this minimizer cannot be selected directly; use predefined prior values instead.
proof.produces: Data-independent prior-variance requirement.

proof.description: Define the predefined grid T={c exp((1-j)/k)|j in N} for sigma_P^2 and assign delta_j=6 delta/(pi^2 j^2); the union bound makes all PAC-Bayes bounds simultaneous with probability at least 1-delta.
proof.produces: A data-independent prior grid and simultaneous confidence event.

proof.description: Set posterior Q=N(w,rho^2 I) and prior mean mu_P=0; under the reduced case, bound the optimal variance numerator.
proof.produces: Upper bound needed to choose a valid grid index j.

proof.description: Choose j=floor(1-k log((rho^2+||w||_2^2/k)/c)) and c=rho^2(1+exp(4n/k)); this ensures j in N and sandwiches sigma_P^2.
proof.produces: Grid variance interval used in the KL bound.

proof.description: Rewrite the KL using the selected sigma_P and Gaussian KL formula.
proof.produces: KL expression ready for interval substitution.

proof.description: Use the lower and upper bounds on sigma_P^2 to upper-bound the KL (equation (10)).
proof.produces: KL upper bound with cancellation available.

proof.description: Cancel the first two terms and simplify the KL logarithm (equation (11)).
proof.produces: Logarithmic KL expression.

proof.description: Using the step-9 assignment sigma_Q=rho (with mu_Q=w and mu_P=0), rewrite equation (11)'s denominator in terms of sigma_Q and factor the ratio to obtain equation (12).
proof.produces: Final KL bound used in PAC-Bayes.

proof.description: Expand the confidence logarithm using delta_j.
proof.produces: Expanded confidence term.

proof.description: Bound the selected floor index by k log(c/(rho^2+||w||_2^2/k)).
proof.produces: Confidence bound involving c and the target variance.

proof.description: Replace the denominator inside the logarithm by rho^2.
proof.produces: Confidence bound with c/rho^2.

proof.description: Substitute c=rho^2(1+exp(4n/k)).
proof.produces: Confidence bound in n and k.

proof.description: Bound log(1+exp(4n/k)) by 2+4n/k.
proof.produces: Polynomial confidence expression.

proof.description: Bound the polynomial expression by the final confidence logarithm.
proof.produces: Final confidence estimate.

proof.description: Insert the KL bound and confidence estimate into PAC-Bayes to obtain the Gaussian-perturbed population/empirical inequality (13).
proof.math: \mathbb E_{\epsilon_i\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma)}[L_{\mathcal D}(w+\epsilon)]\leq\mathbb E_{\epsilon_i\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma)}[L_{\mathcal S}(w+\epsilon)]+\sqrt{\frac{\frac14 k\log\left(1+\frac{\|w\|_2^2}{k\sigma^2}\right)+\frac14+\log\frac n\delta+2\log(6n+3k)}{n-1}}
proof.produces: Expected Gaussian perturbation bound.

proof.description: The Gaussian perturbation law in equation (13) makes ||epsilon||_2^2 a scaled chi-square random variable; invoke Laurent--Massart Lemma 1 for every positive t.
proof.produces: High-probability radius control for Gaussian perturbation.

proof.description: Set t=ln(sqrt(n)) in the tail bound to obtain a 1-1/sqrt(n) event on which ||epsilon||_2^2 is at most sigma^2 k(1+sqrt(ln(n)/k))^2 and satisfies the displayed final <=rho^2 condition.
proof.produces: Perturbations lie in the SAM rho-ball with probability 1-1/sqrt(n).

proof.description: Choose the Gaussian standard deviation used in (13) as the value satisfying the last inequality in the preceding radius display, namely sigma = rho/(sqrt(k)(1+sqrt(ln(n)/k))); this is the sigma substituted in the next step. This parameter choice is derived from the printed radius condition (the paper refers to it as the above value).
proof.ref: Appendix A.1 proof, p. 15 (substitution at lines 985-986)
proof.produces: Sigma substitution \sigma=\rho/(\sqrt{k}(1+\sqrt{\ln(n)/k})) for the PAC-Bayes bound.

proof.description: Substitute this sigma into (13), use the theorem assumption L_D(w)<=E[L_D(w+epsilon)], split the expectation on the radius event, and bound the empirical term by the maximum over the rho-ball.
proof.produces: Intermediate max-over-ball generalization bound.

proof.description: Drop the prefactor on the nonnegative maximum term and combine the additive 1/sqrt(n) with the square-root term, retaining the explicit constants printed in the final display.
proof.produces: Explicit final bound with all constants shown.

proof.description: Absorb the constant logarithmic terms into the paper's O-tilde(1) notation, recovering theorem equation (4).
proof.produces: Theorem 2 conclusion.

key_lemmas.name: Dual_Norm_Inner_Maximizer
key_lemmas.role: Provides the adversarial perturbation used in each SAM update.

proof.description: Define the exact inner maximizer from the SAM objective in equation (1), then apply the first-order Taylor expansion of L_{\mathcal S}(w+epsilon) with respect to epsilon around zero, retaining the constant and linear terms.
proof.math: \epsilon^*(w) \triangleq \arg\max_{\|\epsilon\|_p\leq\rho} L_{\mathcal S}(w+\epsilon) \approx \arg\max_{\|\epsilon\|_p\leq\rho} L_{\mathcal S}(w)+\epsilon^T\nabla_w L_{\mathcal S}(w)
proof.produces: Taylor-approximated inner maximization retaining L_{\mathcal S}(w) and the linear term.

proof.description: Since L_{\mathcal S}(w) is constant with respect to epsilon, discard it from the argmax, yielding the linear dual-norm problem printed in the paper.
proof.math: \arg\max_{\|\epsilon\|_p\leq\rho} L_{\mathcal S}(w)+\epsilon^T\nabla_w L_{\mathcal S}(w) = \arg\max_{\|\epsilon\|_p\leq\rho} \epsilon^T\nabla_w L_{\mathcal S}(w)
proof.produces: Linear dual-norm maximization problem.

proof.description: Use the classical dual norm optimizer to obtain the displayed perturbation formula.
proof.produces: Closed-form first-order adversarial perturbation.

key_lemmas.name: SAM_Gradient_Approximation
key_lemmas.role: Defines the first-order gradient used by Algorithm 1 after dropping Hessian terms.

proof.description: Substitute the perturbation from equation (2) back into the SAM objective of equation (1), then differentiate through the map w+hat epsilon(w) by the chain rule, yielding its Jacobian multiplying the gradient evaluated at the perturbed weights.
proof.produces: Chain-rule form with Jacobian d(w+hat epsilon(w))/dw.

proof.description: Expand the Jacobian d(w+hat epsilon(w))/dw into the identity contribution and the derivative d hat epsilon(w)/dw, producing the direct-gradient term plus the second-order contribution.
proof.produces: Expanded gradient containing the Hessian-vector contribution via d hat epsilon/dw.

proof.description: Drop the second-order terms to obtain the final first-order SAM gradient approximation used by the algorithm.
proof.produces: Gradient approximation g used in Algorithm 1.

key_lemmas.name: McAllester_PAC_Bayes_Bound
key_lemmas.statement_math: \mathbb E_{w\sim\mathcal Q}[L_{\mathcal D}(w)]\leq\mathbb E_{w\sim\mathcal Q}[L_{\mathcal S}(w)]+\sqrt{\frac{\operatorname{KL}(\mathcal Q\|\mathcal P)+\log\frac n\delta}{2(n-1)}}
key_lemmas.role: External PAC-Bayesian inequality used as the starting point of the Appendix proof.

key_lemmas.name: Gaussian_KL_Divergence
key_lemmas.role: Evaluates the PAC-Bayes KL term for isotropic Gaussian prior and posterior.

key_lemmas.name: Laurent_Massart_ChiSquare_Tail
key_lemmas.role: Controls the Gaussian perturbation norm so it falls in the SAM neighborhood with high probability.
